question: Which force causes the trade winds of the southern hemisphere to start blowing from southwest to northeast in India after crossing the equator?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Coriolis force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coriolis force is an apparent force that is observed due to the rotation of the Earth.**
 
• **It deflects the path of moving objects, such as winds and ocean currents, to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.**
 
• In the southern hemisphere, the trade winds start blowing from the southeast towards the equator due to the Coriolis force.
 
• As the winds cross the equator, they are deflected to the right by the Coriolis force, causing them to blow towards the northeast in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational force**

 
 
• It is the force of attraction between two masses, such as the Earth and objects on its surface.
 
• **It is responsible for keeping objects, such as the Moon, in orbit around the Earth and for causing tides.**
 
 
 
• **Magnetic force**
 
 
• **It is the force exerted by magnets and magnetic fields.**
 
• It is responsible for the behavior of compass needles and the Earth's magnetic field, which protects the planet from harmful solar radiation.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal force**
 
 
• **It is the apparent force that is observed due to the rotation of a rotating frame of reference.**
 
• It is often used to explain the behavior of objects in circular motion, but it is not a real force as it is not caused by an interaction between two objects.
